types.name: Walking and treadmill walking
appLabels: Incline walk, picking up the pace
brisk walk outside or around the block

notes.setup: Stand tall with feet supported, familiarise yourself with the start/stop controls and attach a treadmill's emergency cord before starting. Use the actual machine's mounting procedure.
notes.execution: Walk with a natural arm swing and comfortable stride. Adjust speed or incline gradually while keeping the body over the feet rather than hanging from the rails.
notes.alignmentAndRange: Reduce speed or grade if continuous handrail support, overstriding or backward lean is needed. Slow the belt to a stop before stepping off; do not jump onto the side rails to rest.
notes.breathingAndTempo: Breathe continuously and reduce the effort before technique breaks down. Pace labels do not change the movement mechanics or establish a suitable intensity for a particular person.
notes.regression: Use an easier pace, shorter duration, lower resistance or stable low-impact option while keeping the movement controlled.

types.name: Jogging and running

notes.setup: Start on a clear outdoor route or a treadmill at an easy pace with the emergency cord attached and suitable footwear.
notes.execution: Use a comfortable repeatable stride with relaxed shoulders and arms. Build pace gradually and allow a controlled walk/jog recovery between harder efforts.
notes.alignmentAndRange: A fast label does not override technique. Shorten the effort or walk if balance, foot placement or breathing cannot be controlled; treadmill controls and outdoor terrain differ.

types.name: Marching and high knees
appLabels: Brisk walk or march in place

notes.setup: Use a clear nonslip space and a support nearby when balance is limited.
notes.execution: Lift alternate knees with opposite arm swings, placing each foot down under control. Progress from slow marches to brisk marches before a running high-knee version.
notes.alignmentAndRange: Knee height ends before pelvis hiking or leaning backward. A march is a valid low-impact option; do not turn it into jumping just to match a pace label.

types.name: Stationary bike

notes.setup: Adjust and lock the saddle before mounting. At the bottom of the pedal stroke keep a slight knee bend without rocking the hips; secure the feet as the bike requires.
notes.execution: Pedal smoothly with knees following the foot direction, shoulders relaxed and a light supported handle grip. Increase resistance or cadence only while the pelvis remains steady.
notes.alignmentAndRange: Avoid an excessively low seat, locked knees, toe-only reaching or bouncing at high cadence. Stop pedalling and dismount deliberately; console and brake procedures vary by bike.
notes.breathingAndTempo: Breathe continuously and reduce the effort before technique breaks down. Pace labels do not change the movement mechanics or establish a suitable intensity for a particular person.
notes.regression: Use an easier pace, shorter duration, lower resistance or stable low-impact option while keeping the movement controlled.

types.name: Air bike

notes.setup: Set and lock the saddle using the model's instructions, check foot straps and understand how the linked moving handles/pedals behave.
notes.execution: Coordinate arm push/pull and leg drive through a smooth rhythm without trunk rocking. Start gently because the flywheel resistance rises with effort.
notes.alignmentAndRange: The upright-bike source supports saddle fit only; linked-handle mechanics are an equipment adaptation. Keep hands and feet clear of moving parts and let the mechanism slow before leaving.

types.name: Rowing machine

notes.setup: Set footrests and straps so the feet are secure, grip lightly with wrists flat and choose manageable resistance before increasing effort.
notes.execution: At the catch keep arms long and hinge from the hips. Drive legs first, then open the trunk and finish with the arms toward the lower ribs. Recover arms first, hinge forward, then bend the knees.
notes.alignmentAndRange: Do not bend the arms early, overcompress the catch, round the back or lean far backward at the finish. Faster pace should come from a cleaner stronger stroke rather than rushed recovery.
notes.breathingAndTempo: Breathe continuously and reduce the effort before technique breaks down. Pace labels do not change the movement mechanics or establish a suitable intensity for a particular person.
notes.regression: Use an easier pace, shorter duration, lower resistance or stable low-impact option while keeping the movement controlled.

types.name: Elliptical

notes.setup: Use the stationary supports to mount, place both feet securely on the pedals and begin at low resistance; learn the stop behaviour before increasing pace.
notes.execution: Stand tall with ribs over the pelvis, follow the pedal path smoothly and use moving handles only while the trunk remains controlled.
notes.alignmentAndRange: Avoid hanging bodyweight on the rails, lifting the heels excessively to chase speed or looking down continuously. Keep hands on safe supports until the pedals settle for dismounting.

types.name: Stair climber

notes.setup: Identify the stop control, mount using stable rails and start at a low step rate with the feet securely placed.
notes.execution: Step one foot at a time with a controlled forward-facing posture and light rail contact for balance. Place enough of the foot on each tread for secure pressure.
notes.alignmentAndRange: Do not support most bodyweight through the rails, skip steps or add backward/sideways patterns in this baseline. Reduce speed before the tread depth becomes difficult to judge.

types.name: Jump rope
appLabels: jump rope intervals (30 s on, 30 s off)

notes.setup: Use a rope length and open area that allow a clear arc above and around the body; begin with isolated small jumps or rope-free rhythm practice.
notes.execution: Keep elbows near the sides and use small wrist-driven circles with low soft jumps, landing under the body with knees unlocked. Reset deliberately after a trip.
notes.alignmentAndRange: The retrieved ACE reference is a brief drill description, so exact rope fitting remains practical-review work. Avoid high tuck jumps or locked-knee landings merely to clear the rope.

types.name: Jumping jacks

notes.setup: Begin in a clear space with feet together or hip-width and arms relaxed.
notes.execution: Make a small jump to widen the feet as the arms rise through a comfortable overhead arc, then return softly. For a step jack, move one foot out at a time without jumping.
notes.alignmentAndRange: Keep knees tracking with the feet and reduce arm height if overhead motion pinches. The step version preserves a lower-impact option without forcing a fast rebound.

types.name: Shadow boxing

notes.setup: Use clear space and a balanced staggered stance with soft knees, hands near the face and no external hand weights.
notes.execution: Practise relaxed controlled punches, returning to guard between actions and moving the feet without crossing. Let feet and hips turn together for a rotational punch.
notes.alignmentAndRange: Do not lock the elbows forcefully, swing punches through an exaggerated back twist or sacrifice guard/footwork to match a fast-finish label. This is noncontact practice.
